# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).
data.title: Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

# F3 — Auto-sync isolation: pane never stalls on `wl sync`

## Background

Auto-sync spawns `wl sync` (≈ 36 s on a ~100 MB DB) fire-and-forget every 60 s.
Parent AC 3 requires that while a long sync is in flight the pane stays
responsive: no lock wait, no event-loop stall, no "hanging" indication beyond a
brief non-blocking status notice. The current single-flight + heartbeat +
`--if-idle` guards (auto-sync.ts) bound spawns but do not yet guarantee the
pane never competes with or waits on a long-running sync (IO contention with
refresh reads, process-group/PID effects, no UI notice). F2 profiles where the
~36 s goes and whether a `wl sync` fix is a separate item (scope guard).

## Target outcome

A refresh completes within budget while a long `wl sync` is in flight in the
background, with a non-blocking status notice shown; the pane never waits on
the sync lock or its process.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a simulated/hooked long ~36 s `wl sync` in flight (F1 harness), a
  concurrent default-view refresh completes within the parent AC 2 budget and
  blocks the TUI event loop ≤ 200 ms aggregate (parent AC 1); asserted by an
  automated test in the default suite.
- The auto-sync spawn is verified off the TUI event loop and the pane shows a
  non-blocking status notice ("syncing…") that never blocks input; no "hanging"
  UI state beyond the notice (parent AC 3).
- No lock contention: an in-flight sync does not hold/reset the same SQLite
  handle or filesystem lock the pane's in-process refresh scope uses; a refresh
  never waits for a sync to finish (asserted with in-flight instrumentation:
  e.g. start time monotonic, no wait gap equal to remaining sync time).
- Existing guarantees preserved: single-flight, cross-pane heartbeat skip,
  `--if-idle`, 60 s interval, no concurrent sync spawns (parent AC 6); the F1
  zero-spawn-when-idle assertion still passes.
- If F2 concludes a `wl sync` perf fix is a separate work item, this item stays
  limited to pane-side isolation and references that item — no scope creep.

## Minimal Implementation

- Route auto-sync through the same background-task runtime used elsewhere
  (`packages/herdr/src` background helpers) with explicit event-loop decoupling
  and a tiny status model the pane renders without blocking.
- Add in-flight instrumentation (process start + PID + elapsed) so a refresh
  can verify non-interference; extend F1 harness with a "sync in flight"
  scenario.
- Add the non-blocking status notice and back it with the automated
  responsiveness test above.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — spawn path, single-flight, heartbeat.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — refresh orchestration + status rendering.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — in-flight sync scenario.

## Deliverables

- Off-loop auto-sync with status notice, in-flight instrumentation, an
  automated responsiveness-under-sync test, and updated
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` notes.

## Dependencies

- F2 profile results (plus F1 harness).
data.title: F3 — Auto-sync isolation: pane never stalls on `wl sync`

# F4 — In-process dependency and child reads on expand

## Background

Expanding a node still triggers per-item `wl dep list` (hydrator, ≈ 0.4 s each)
and single-parent `wl list --parent` spawns (`fetchChildrenForItem`); each
spawn costs 0.5–0.9 s and ~130–145 MB RSS. The batching in-process path already
exists for multi-parent fetches (`fetchChildrenForItems` via the refresh
scope) but the single-parent and per-hydrator-item paths still spawn. Parent
AC 2 bounds refresh end-to-end to ≤ ~1.5 s including per-expand child fetches,
and AC 5 bounds aggregate spawn RSS.

## Target outcome

Expanding a node (or hydrating its deps) performs zero `wl` spawns on the
large-DB path: all child/dependency reads are served in-process through the
one refresh-scoped SQLite connection, with the existing fail-open CLI fallback
unchanged for correctness edge cases.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Expanding a parent performs no `wl list --parent` / `wl dep list` spawn (F1
  spawn-count assertion) when the in-process path is available; child and
  dependency rows match the CLI's ordering, fields, depth and enrichment
  semantics on a ~2,600-item fixture.
- Hydrator dependency lookups use the in-process/refresh-scope read (or a
  bounded batched lookup) instead of one `wl dep list` spawn per item; the
  hydrator timeout behaviour from WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P is preserved.
- Fail-open preserved: when no worklog dir / SQLite file / `@worklog/shared` is
  available, or a stored audit fingerprint requires CLI enrichment, behaviour
  falls back to spawns exactly as today (existing `fetcher-inprocess` and
  `worklist-expand-refresh` tests still green).
- The one-open-per-refresh scope is kept — no new per-helper DB opens are
  introduced (parent AC constraints).
- Existing Herdr + TUI suites pass with zero-spawn-when-idle preserved (parent
  AC 6).

## Minimal Implementation

- Route `fetchChildrenForItem` through the shared batch/in-process reader when
  a scope is available; keep its signature and fail-open.
- Convert per-item hydrator `wl dep list` calls to a batched in-process dep
  read within the refresh scope (grouping visible items into one pass), with
  fail-open for the fingerprint/enrichment cases.
- Extend F1 harness assertions (expanded-node spawn counts) and the
  `fetchChildrenForItem/ForItems` in-process tests.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — single-parent fetch + batch reader + scope.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — per-item `wl dep list` calls.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — expand orchestration.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-inprocess.test.ts`, `worklist-expand-refresh.test.ts` — extend.

## Deliverables

- Spawn-free expand + hydrator dep reads on the in-process path, updated
  fail-open tests, F1 harness assertions green, and a completion comment with
  large-DB timing/spawn deltas vs baseline.

## Dependencies

- F2 profile results (confirms dep/child reads as a cost driver) and F1
  harness baselines.
data.title: F4 — In-process dependency and child reads on expand

# F5 — Bound `wl` spawn memory and concurrency for a single pane

## Background

Each surviving `wl worklist`/`wl list` spawn peaks at ~130–145 MB RSS on a
~100 MB DB (intake measurements). Parent AC 5 is satisfied either by reducing
per-spawn memory below a documented budget or by bounding concurrent spawns so
aggregate RSS for a single pane stays under a documented ceiling (e.g.
≤ ~300 MB). F2 determines where the memory goes and whether the `wl worklist`
payload can be trimmed without breaking its documented contract.

## Target outcome

A documented, enforced per-pane RSS/spawn budget that guarantees parent AC 5
at large-DB scale, without regressing small-DB behaviour or the consolidated
single-read default view.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-spawn or aggregate budget confirmed: measured peak aggregate RSS for a
  single pane during a full refresh (F1 harness, full scale) is at or below a
  documented ceiling (target ≤ ~300 MB as in parent AC 5), OR per-spawn peak is
  reduced below the ~130–145 MB observed baseline and the reduced number is
  documented as the new budget.
- Based on F2's evidence, either: (a) a payload trim on `wl worklist` (drop
  unused fields/streaming) with the documented payload contract preserved or
  explicitly revised and tested, or (b) a documented spawn cap (e.g. N
  concurrent `wl` spawns, queueing/deferred reads) whose aggregate RSS is
  asserted by an automated test — without waiting under the event loop.
- The budget and its enforcement are documented in
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` (parent AC 5 "documented budget").
- No regression to small worklogs and no change to the consolidated
  single-read default-view norm; zero-spawn-when-idle preserved (parent AC 6).
- All remaining `wl` spawns execute off the TUI event loop, and deferred/
  queued reads never block input: the F1 harness event-loop aggregation stays
  within the parent AC 1 ≤ ~200 ms bound with a spawn-heavy fixture (intake
  candidate 4).
- No new heavy dependencies (parent constraints) — prefer reuse of the
  in-process SQLite read path over new spawns.

## Minimal Implementation

- Apply the F2-validated memory fix (payload trim with contract test, or
  streaming) and/or add a concurrency semaphore around `wl` spawns in the
  fetch path with queued fallback reads.
- Add F1 harness assertions for aggregate RSS, spawn count, and event-loop
  blocking at full scale.
- Ensure every remaining spawn is dispatched off the TUI event loop (existing
  background-task runtime) with a bounded queue; assert no input-lock via the
  harness.
- Update docs; record before/after numbers in the completion comment.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — spawn path, exec seam, spawn cap.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — payload build (if trim chosen).
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — RSS/spawn assertions.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — budget documentation.

## Deliverables

- Enforced spawn/RSS budget with automated assertion, validated memory fix
  (trim or cap) per F2 evidence, docs, and measured before/after numbers.

## Dependencies

- F2 (memory breakdown + payload-contract decision), F1 harness.
data.title: F5 — Bound `wl` spawn memory and concurrency for a single pane

# F6 — Single, cheap in-process SQLite open per refresh

## Background

In-process SQLite reads on a ~100 MB DB carry a non-trivial open cost (open +
pragmas + FTS DDL ~46–70 ms measured in earlier work; the one-open-per-refresh
scope from WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B exists to amortise it). Surviving per-helper
opens, read-only open DDL, and connection reuse across ticks are the remaining
levers. Parent AC 2 (≤ ~1.5 s default-view refresh p95) and AC 1 (no event-loop
stall) constrain this cost; F2 quantifies its share.

## Target outcome

A default-view refresh performs at most one cheap in-process SQLite open
(shared across all refresh helpers, read-only, minimal/no DDL when already
initialised), and the open cost is small enough that it never threatens the
refresh budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An automated test (F1 harness, full scale) asserts a default-view refresh
  performs at most one in-process DB open per refresh and that helper reads
  reuse that single connection (no per-helper open).
- The read-only open path is measured and documented: open+pragmas cost is
  recorded after the change (target: eliminate the ~46–70 ms FTS-DDL hit on
  already-initialised stores, e.g. by skipping DDL when schema/version already
  present), with numbers below the refresh budget headroom.
- Open is verified off the TUI event loop / within the existing refresh scope
  (parent AC 1); any background warm-up does not overlap a visible refresh in a
  blocking way.
- Fail-open preserved: a read-only open failure degrades to the existing `wl`
  spawn fallback; no change to the hydrator's core behaviour or scheduler
  (parent constraints).
- Existing Herdr + TUI suites pass; zero-spawn-when-idle preserved (parent
  AC 6).

## Minimal Implementation

- Refactor the refresh-scope open to: one shared connection per refresh across
  all helpers, read-only pragma set, and schema/DDL only when required
  (version check); verify `@worklog/shared` `WorklogDatabase` surface honours
  a read-only/no-DDL mode or the skip is done at the caller.
- Add harness timing for the open step; update docs budgeting the open cost.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — refresh scope + `InProcessRefreshScope` open.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `WorklogDatabase` open/DDL path.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — open-cost timing.

## Deliverables

- One-cheap-open-per-refresh with automated single-open + timing assertions,
  fail-open tests green, and documented open-cost numbers.

## Dependencies

- F2 (quantifies open cost share), F1 harness.
data.title: F6 — Single, cheap in-process SQLite open per refresh

# F7 — Large-DB responsiveness verification at scale

## Background

The parent's ACs are acceptance criteria for the whole pane behaviour at scale.
F1–F6 each deliver targeted fixes and tests; this item is the end-to-end
verification slice that confirms every parent AC holds together on a
~2,600-item / ~100 MB fixture after all changes, including the AC 4
write→reflect re-verification (extending WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN to large-DB
scale) and AC 6's full-suite no-regression gate.

## Target outcome

One reproducible end-to-end evidence run (documented commands + test suite)
that every parent acceptance criterion 1–6 is met at large-DB scale.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Pane stays responsive during refresh:** a default-view refresh does not block the TUI event loop for more than ~200 ms of perceived lag in aggregate (verified with an automated test harness or measured timing on a large fixture DB) — keystrokes/commands process promptly while a refresh is in flight. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Single-figure refresh cost on large DBs:** a default-view refresh end-to-end (event → data load → render) is bounded to ≤ ~1.5 s wall-clock p95 on a DB of ~2,600 items / ~100 MB, including per-expand child fetches; the consolidated `wl worklist` single-read path stays the norm — no regression to multi-spawn refreshes. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Auto-sync cannot stall the pane:** while a long `wl sync` (measured ~36 s on the 100 MB DB) is in flight in the background, the pane remains responsive — no lock wait, no event-loop stall, at most a brief non-blocking status notice. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Change reflection latency:** after a `wl` write, the pane reflects the change within ~2 s p95 via the event-driven watch path at large-DB scale. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Reduced memory footprint:** a refresh's spawned `wl` processes peak at no more than a documented per-spawn budget below the ~130–145 MB/spawn observed baseline, OR concurrent spawns are bounded so aggregate RSS for a single pane stays under a documented ceiling (e.g. ≤ ~300 MB). (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **No regressions:** the full Herdr plugin + TUI test suites pass; the zero-spawn-when-idle guarantee and event-driven watch semantics are preserved. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)

- All measured numbers are quoted in the completion comment against the F1 baseline; if any criterion is not met, the blocking fix item is referenced with its data rather than accepted silently.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the F1 harness with an end-to-end "all ACs" report mode aggregating
  every metric into one JSON report plus a human summary.
- Drive the event-driven write→reflect measurement at full scale (reusing the
  watch path from WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN) and assert AC 4 at large-DB scale.
- Run the full suite + full-scale harness, record the report comment, and mark
  this item (and via parent workflow, the parent) ready once green.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — end-to-end AC report mode.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — metrics under test (spawn/refresh path).
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — in-flight sync scenario under test.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — final numbers.

## Deliverables

- End-to-end AC evidence report (comment + checked-in harness mode), full-suite
  green, and the parent ready for review.

## Dependencies

- F3, F4, F5, F6 (all targeted fixes landed).
data.title: F7 — Large-DB responsiveness verification at scale
